title: Interplay between stress granule-like structures and nuclear RNA export in a heat shock-specific manner.
data_url: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42621734#supplementary-material (Supplementary Tables_revised_v2.xlsx, Table S4); raw data: SRA PRJNA1305664, PRJNA1474590; ProteomeXchange PXD080458

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the supplement; parsed Supplementary Table S4 in Python: 4,241 unique locus IDs (4,240 with data), 9 spectral-count columns (whole-cell lysate, stress-granule-enriched fraction, bead-only control; 3 replicates each), 268-824 zeros per column, no duplicate IDs. Downloaded the Fusarium graminearum proteome FASTA (protein sequences, 4.6 MB, 14,202 entries) from Ensembl Fungi and joined it: 4,208/4,240 (99.2%) IDs matched, and stated molecular weight tracks sequence length at r=0.999, confirming the join is correct. Computed column-sum-normalised enrichment: median enriched/total ratio 1.23, 2,552 proteins above the authors' 0.7 cutoff, replicate agreement of per-replicate log2 enrichment r=0.93-0.94. Ran the paper's own positive control: the 8 literature-validated stress-granule proteins in Table S2 sit at enrichment percentiles 0.20-0.86 (mean 0.54), and Pab1 (the bait protein used to define the granules) is at the 52nd percentile and is NOT enriched over the bead-only control (log2 SG/bead = -0.20). Also measured the confound: log2 enrichment correlates -0.53 with whole-cell abundance.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the numbers are total spectral counts normalised across samples (Scaffold v5.0.1, Proteome Discoverer v2.4.1.15), that the enriched/total cutoff of 0.7 was chosen empirically to capture known stress-granule proteins, that the proteomics was done under heat shock, and that the RNA-sequencing results (granule-associated transcripts, nuclear retention scores) exist - those processed tables are not deposited anywhere, only raw reads in SRA.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary zip (1.7 MB) downloaded freely from Europe PMC and opened; no login or application. Verified in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Measured spectral counts in the granule fraction are columns; the enrichment label is one arithmetic ratio within the same table (no join, no inference across sources). Verified.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are not in the table, but one bulk FASTA download from Ensembl Fungi matched 99.2% of IDs in a single join. Verified by doing it.

a4_units_stated.note: Units (total spectral counts, normalised across samples) are in the methods, not in the table header; molecular weight given in kDa. Column sums differ 60k-112k, so the deposited values look pre-normalisation.

a5_enough_rows.note: 4,240 proteins with data; 2,256 have >=10 summed counts in both fractions. Counted in the file.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; ESM-2 embeddings for 4,208 sequences are the only real cost. Verified sizes.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No contradiction found, but the paper never states how many proteins were quantified, so there is nothing to confirm against the 4,241 rows I counted.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a physical measurement (liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry spectral counts), not another model's output. But it is confounded with protein abundance (r=-0.53, measured by me), so abundance-driven leakage is a live risk.

B1.why: One Excel table plus one bulk proteome FASTA; join verified at 99.2% on transcript ID.

B2.why: xlsx with a two-row merged header; parsed after specifying header rows. Checked in file.

B3.why: Single assay and lab, but deposited counts are not column-normalised (sums 60k-112k); one-line fix.

B4.why: 268-824 zeros per column make ratios undefined; depth filter keeps 2,256 of 4,240. Counted.

B5.why: 4,241 unique locus IDs, zero duplicates in the file.

B6.why: Headers self-explanatory, but units only in methods and no README or cutoff column.

C1.why: Transfer question is informative in principle, but a failed positive control makes any negative result uninterpretable.

C2.why: MaGS/MaGSeq, PSAP, PSPire, catGRANULE, PScore exist and are open; none trained on fungal granule proteomes.

C3.why: Diversity angle (first filamentous-fungal granule proteome) is real but undermined by label specificity.

C4.why: Granule purification plus mass spectrometry and GFP tagging is slow, lab-based and expensive.

C5.why: Obvious dummy (abundance alone, r=-0.53 measured) plus runnable open predictors PSAP and PSPire.

D1.why: ESM-2, an open-weight protein language model, matches amino-acid sequence input exactly.

D2.why: 4,208 sequences, median 431 residues: embeddings cached once on CPU, then a linear head.

D3.why: ESM-2 weights are MIT-licensed; Ensembl Fungi data is open.

E1.why: Sequences available, so 30% identity clustering with held-out clusters is constructible.

E2.why: Thousands of sequence clusters and Pfam families among 4,208 proteins; ample groups.

E3.why: Global mean, length-only (r=0.08) and abundance-only (r=-0.53) dummies all computable; I computed them.

E4.why: Three replicates per fraction; per-replicate log2 enrichment agrees at r=0.93-0.94. Measured.

E5.why: Ran it and it failed: the paper's 8 validated granule proteins average the 54th percentile of enrichment.

E6.why: Label shuffling, abundance-only ablation and random features are all straightforward here.

E7.why: Yeast and mammalian stress-granule proteomes (MSGP, RNAgranuleDB, PhaSepDB) give an independent label set.

E8.why: Paper reports no quantitative model number, protein count or AUC that could be reproduced on this data.

G1.why: Standard Ensembl Fungi transcript IDs present; one mapped cleanly to UniProt I1RWX5 when tested.

G2.why: AlphaFold DB structures, PhaSepDB/CD-CODE condensate sets and InterPro domains are all named partners.

G3.why: Transcript-to-protein join is one-to-one and verified at 99.2%; one gene, one protein in this fungus.

G4.why: Combination asks whether condensate recruitment rules hold across a billion years of fungal evolution.

H1.why: Background proteins and bead control give negatives, but 10,000 undetected proteins are unlabelled.

H2.why: One lab, one strain, one species, one stress (heat shock), one time point. From paper and file.

H3.why: Honest claim is writable in one sentence, and it is narrow; see honest_claim_h3.

H4.why: Paper admits the 0.7 cutoff is empirical, but never flags the abundance confound or weak bait enrichment.

I1.why: Condensate-predictor developers (GraPES/MaGS authors) and Fusarium head-blight labs are named audiences.

I2.why: A ranking could nominate proteins for GFP tagging, but label quality makes acting on it risky.

I3.why: Precision in the top 50 matches the tagging decision, but ground truth is unreliable.

I4.why: Abundance alone explains much of the label (r=-0.53); disorder content may take the rest.

J1.why: Protein language model embeddings, identity-clustered splits and cross-species transfer are real ML.

J2.why: Known granule proteins and yeast orthologs give objective sanity anchors for plausibility.

J3.why: Cleaned sequence-joined table is shareable, but its value drops once the label fails its control.

J4.why: Bounded: about three weeks, since embedding and cross-validation are hours, not days.

J5.why: Kill condition statable (no gain over abundance baseline in one week) but not written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: MaGS / MaGSeq (GraPES web server, Nucleic Acids Research 2022) - predicts whether a protein localises to stress granules
existing_models.score_and_split: MaGSeq reports area under the ROC curve 0.76 (human) and 0.77 (yeast) on held-out test proteins; precomputed scores published for several proteomes
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: MaGS needs experimentally measured features (abundance, phosphorylation sites), so MaGSeq was built to be sequence-only; the authors say models are optimised for mammals and yeast and only 'in principle' apply to other eukaryotes

existing_models.name: PSAP (Cell Reports 2021) - random forest scoring condensate-forming propensity from amino-acid composition
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as a proteome-wide classifier trained on known phase-separating proteins; I did not retrieve its exact held-out number
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation beyond the curated human/yeast positives used for training

existing_models.name: PSPire (Nature Communications 2024) - gradient-boosted classifier using residue- and structure-level features
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to outperform earlier predictors on proteins lacking intrinsically disordered regions; a 2025 benchmark cites its area under the ROC curve near 0.84 on that task
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Phase separation in proteins without disordered regions, and dependence on predicted structures

existing_models.name: catGRANULE and PScore (2016-2017 biophysical propensity scores)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used as the comparison baselines that MaGSeq beat at 0.76/0.77 area under the ROC curve
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Both rely on single biophysical signals (RNA-binding propensity, pi-pi contacts) and miss condensate proteins lacking them

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model, esm2_t33_650M or the smaller t12_35M checkpoint)
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop; ~2-4 h one-time embedding for 4,208 sequences at the 650M checkpoint, minutes at 35M

integration.partner_dataset: AlphaFold DB predicted structures (via UniProt) plus curated condensate membership sets (PhaSepDB, CD-CODE, MSGP mammalian stress granule proteome)
integration.join_key: Ensembl Fungi transcript/gene ID -> UniProt accession; sequence-level comparison needs no ID join
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do the sequence and structure features that recruit a protein into a stress granule hold across a billion years of fungal evolution, or is granule composition lineage-specific?

controls.positive_control: The 8 literature-validated granule proteins in Supplementary Table S2 (Pab1, Pub1, Pbp1, Ngr1, eIF4E, Lsm7, Bre5, Ubp3) must rank near the top. I ran this and it FAILED: mean percentile 0.54, Pab1 (the bait) at 0.52 and not enriched over the bead-only control.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle enrichment labels and confirm collapse to the per-abundance-bin mean; train on whole-cell abundance alone (already r=-0.53) to show how much of the label is abundance.
controls.external_validation: Yeast and mammalian stress-granule proteomes (MSGP, RNAgranuleDB, PhaSepDB) as an independently measured label set in other species.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here could only claim to predict which of the 4,240 proteins detectable by mass spectrometry in one heat-shocked Fusarium graminearum strain are recovered more abundantly in a Pab1-based granule pellet than in whole-cell lysate - a quantity that, in this dataset, does not rank the authors' own validated granule proteins above the median.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino-acid sequence to predict how strongly it is pulled down with heat-shock stress granules in a crop-pathogen fungus.
plain_idea.train_on: One amino-acid sequence per protein (median 431 residues) for 4,208 Fusarium graminearum proteins, matched 99.2% from the paper's proteomics table to the Ensembl Fungi proteome.
plain_idea.predict: The log ratio of mass-spectrometry spectral counts in the purified stress-granule-like fraction versus whole-cell lysate under heat shock, measured in triplicate (replicate agreement r=0.93).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups who build condensate predictors have only human and yeast training data, so a fungal test set would show whether their models transfer; fungal biologists would get a shortlist of proteins to tag and image.

more_or_better_data.why: 4,240 quantitatively measured proteins in triplicate from a filamentous plant-pathogenic fungus, a lineage absent from MaGS/PSAP/PSPire training sets (human and yeast curated positives, typically hundreds of proteins). But it is one species and one condition, and the measurement does not cleanly separate known granule proteins.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate spectral counts give a per-protein measurement variance (replicate enrichment r=0.93), which MaGS, PSAP and PSPire do not provide since their labels are curated binary memberships. I judged this from their published descriptions, not by running them.

models_beatable.why: MaGSeq (2022) is a generalised linear model on handcrafted features at area under the ROC curve 0.76-0.77; PSAP (2021) is a composition random forest; catGRANULE/PScore are 2016-2017 biophysical scores. None uses a protein language model, and 2025 ProtT5-based work already reports higher numbers.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Existing predictors can be run as baselines, but the extra data (yeast and mammalian curated granule proteomes) measures a different quantity - binary curated membership in another species - by different assays, so the same-quantity and same-split conditions both fail.

ml_idea: Freeze ESM-2 embeddings of 4,208 Fusarium graminearum proteins and fit a head to predict log2 stress-granule-fraction enrichment, with 30%-identity-clustered held-out splits, and benchmark MaGSeq/PSAP/PSPire out-of-distribution on a fungal granule proteome. Attractive on paper - but the label fails the paper's own positive control, so the project would measure pellet background rather than granule biology.

effort.compute_note: Sizes and row counts timed directly (the whole table parses in under a second); embedding hours estimated at roughly 0.5-3 s per sequence for ESM-2 650M on an Apple Silicon CPU for 4,208 sequences of median length 431, not timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Rank the 8 validated granule proteins from Supplementary Table S2 by the measured enrichment. I ran it: mean percentile 0.54, Pab1 bait at 0.52 with no enrichment over the bead control. This kills the project in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: The data is small, clean and genuinely easy to use - 4,240 proteins, 99.2% joined to sequences in one step, replicate agreement r=0.93 - and the cross-species transfer question is a good one. But the label does not survive its own positive control: the eight stress-granule proteins the authors themselves validated sit at an average 54th percentile of the measured enrichment, and Pab1, the bait protein that defines the structures, is at the 52nd percentile and shows no enrichment over the bead-only control. The authors' own cutoff (enriched/total ratio >=0.7) labels 2,552 of 4,240 proteins as putative components, and the enrichment correlates -0.53 with whole-cell abundance. A model fitted to this target would learn what pellets with beads, not what joins a stress granule, and a benchmark against it would be uninterpretable. The RNA-sequencing side (granule-associated transcripts, nuclear retention scores), which looks more interesting, is deposited only as raw reads in SRA with no processed tables.
